round1.position: Refuted, major. The return used an impossible patient-years figure inside the window, computed break-even on revenue instead of contribution, rested on non-public Part D rows and assumed full capture; narrow to a controlled pilot with a scale-up gate.

round2.position: Refuted, major, narrowed. Concedes the program already runs and that competition is cited; holds the arithmetic errors and the need for control sites; adopts the decider's smaller budget in two tranches with matched control sites and a month-12 starts gate at break-even.

round1.position: Refuted, major. round2.position: Refuted, major, narrowed. Concedes the CFO arithmetic and the need for a control design; holds the already-running framing, the promo fixes and that the starts gate is internal only; adopts the CFO's larger controlled pilot.

steps.reason: Both lenses refuted the move as written and both narrowed it toward the same structure. Conceded by both: the program already runs (2026 proxy, page eighty-one), the return arithmetic was wrong (patient-years inside the window and a revenue-based break-even), the non-public Part D rows must go, and lift needs a control design. Still disagreeing: the budget size and whether the starts gate is a kill signal or an internal checkpoint (see unresolved). Settled from the source: the per-patient value is re-based on the CMS 2024 annual row and the Q2 2026 10-Q product table (page thirty-eight), with the decider's three label additions (dosing, drug-interaction and lactation sections) and claims-map rows. Ruled narrowed to the two-tranche, control-site scale-up written in the move; this is unrefuted on the corrected math, not confirmed, since the starts response is untested.
